extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (patent attorneys/agents), OED staff, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and criteria the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) uses to evaluate practitioner misconduct, the legal bases for jurisdiction, examples of disqualifying conduct (e.g., false expense claims), and the sanctions/rehabilitation framework (suspension, probation, reinstatement, publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory/regulatory provisions provide the legal basis for OED investigations, settlement approvals, and issuance of Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof in stipulated facts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a disciplinary proceeding were brought, evidence would be presented that would 'clearly and convincingly establish' the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED uses the clear-and-convincing evidence standard when presenting factual bases in stipulated/settled matters; language indicates sufficiency of evidence for the allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting requests for reimbursement of expenses the practitioner knew he had not actually paid is cited as conduct violating § 11.804(c). Examples and quantified instances (multiple false reimbursement claims and amounts) illustrate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts and omissions that don't fall squarely under a specific rule can still violate § 11.804(i) if they adversely reflect on fitness; the Final Order applies this to the respondent's misconduct in addition to § 11.804(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office for two (2) years beginning on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension means the practitioner is barred from practicing before the USPTO for the specified period and remains suspended until the OED Director grants reinstatement under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remain suspended until reinstatement petition is granted (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic at the end of the suspension period; the petitioner must satisfy § 11.60 requirements and obtain OED Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period after reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a probationary period of twelve (12) months commencing on the date the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation imposes additional monitoring and conditions; violation of probation procedures may trigger immediate further suspension proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause process for probation violation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period, if OED continues to believe there was noncompliance, OED will deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to twelve (12) months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension-review timing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the Order to Show Cause and Respondent seeks review of the suspension, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not stay the suspension; suspension remains in effect during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice must include essential facts (identity, suspension length and probation, summary of misconduct, rules violated, cooperation) and the FOIA Reading Room posting makes the decision publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing any further complaint or evidence of same or similar misconduct, and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used as an aggravating factor, to rebut representations by or on behalf of Respondent, or in connection with reconsideration requests under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration, review, and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement can include express waivers of procedural and appellate remedies, which removes those avenues from the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial financial actions and restitution considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent repaid the Firm partial restitution ($100,000 + later $20,000), forfeited his capital account and portion of monthly draw, and the Firm reimbursed clients for fraudulent charges passed on to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of restitution and other remedial financial steps are documented and treated as considerations in the sanctioning/settlement context (mitigating factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation, candor, and remedial efforts as mitigating considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent fully and diligently cooperated with OED's investigation, responded thoroughly and candidly in a timely manner, maintained active communication, voluntarily sought assistance in understanding why he committed misconduct, and has been candid about efforts to prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly notes cooperation and remedial efforts; such behavior is used as mitigating factors in settlement and sanction formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and Final Order approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Parties submitted a Proposed Settlement Agreement to the Under Secretary/USPTO Director for approval; the Agreement resolves all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts and is approved by the Director as a Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters may be resolved by negotiated settlement which, when approved by the Director, becomes a Final Order with binding sanction terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can include terms allocating costs, often resulting in each side bearing its own expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct constituting violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factual examples include submitting receipts for airfare/hotel/restaurant for trips not taken and submitting receipts for purchases that were refunded to obtain reimbursement for expenses not actually incurred; counts and monetary totals are enumerated (392 false requests totaling $361,646.47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order uses these concrete examples to illustrate the kinds of dishonest conduct that violate professional rules and justify disciplinary sanctions.
